    AI Overview
    "Go Blue!" is the iconic rallying cry for the University of Michigan Wolverines, representing a rich tradition in athletics and academics since the 1860s. It also refers to the Go Blue Guarantee, a program offering free tuition for qualified in-state students. It signifies school pride, community, and excellence. 
    Key Aspects of "Go Blue" 
    • Athletics Tradition: The phrase is famously associated with Michigan football and basketball, with players touching the "Go Blue" banner when entering Michigan Stadium.
    • Origin: The phrase is believed to have originated in the 1950s, popularized at Michigan hockey games
      .
    • Go Blue Guarantee: A significant financial aid initiative for Michigan residents, providing free or reduced tuition for up to four years.
    • University-Wide Campaign: "Those Who Go Blue" is a campaign that connects students, alumni, and fans. 
    Whether in athletics or academics, "Go Blue" serves as a rallying cry for the Michigan community, including the Ann Arbor, Dearborn, and Flint campuses.

    AI Overview
    "Go Blue" is
    the primary rallying cry and cheer for the University of Michigan Wolverines, representing the school's colors (maize and blue) and expressing support for its sports teams. It is also the name of the "Go Blue Guarantee," a financial aid program that covers tuition for qualifying in-state students. 
    Key Aspects of "Go Blue": 
    • Athletic Cheer: Coined in the 1950s, it serves as a rallying cry for all U-M fans and teams.
    • School Spirit: It signifies support for the University of Michigan athletics and the institution's community.
    • "Go Blue" Guarantee:
      A financial aid program offering free or reduced tuition to Michigan residents with family incomes of
      or less (subject to asset limits).
    • "Let's Go Blue": A popular song played at sporting events that often follows the cheer. 
    The phrase is widely used by students, alumni, and fans to show pride in the university.
